column2: Matter is something that occupies space and has mass.

column3: Matter is made-up of very small particles.
Molecule constituting a matter are very small.
These particles of molecules are called atoms.
Particles of matter are always in motion & motion of particles increases with increase in temperature.
Particles of matter are attracted to each other by intermolecular force, called as intermolecular force of attraction (F.A.)
Inter mixing of particles of 2 different types of matter on their own is called diffusion.

column4: Solid: Has definite shape, distinct boundaries and fixed volume.
Liquid: Do not have fixed shape, but has fix volume.
Gas: Neither has fixed shape nor has fixed volume.
Melting or fusion: Solid to liquid.
Melting Point: Solid melts to become liquid.
Latent heat of fusion: The amount of heat energy required to change 1 Kg of solid into liquid at atmospheric pressure at its melting point is called latent heat of fusion.
Freezing Point: Liquid freezes into solid.
Boiling Point: Liquid heats and becomes gas.
Latent heat of vaporization: The amount of head energy required to change 1 Kg of liquid into gas at atmospheric pressure at its boiling point is called latent heat of vaporization.
Condensation Point: Gas gets converted into liquid.
Gases can be liquified by applying pressure and reduce in temperature.

column5: In liquid a small fraction of particles having higher kinetic energy is able to break away from F.A. and get converted into vapour. This is called evaporation.

column4: Evaporation causes cooling: When liquid evaporates it causes cooling in its surrounding area.
